scenarios.title: untrusted input crosses a boundary without validation at browser-to-Express API when anonymous caller controls a request
scenarios.domain: Architecture, assets, trust boundaries and threat modeling
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: trust-boundary confusion or unsafe data flow
scenarios.potentialImpact: Potential medium-class impact to affected data, identity, or service; reachability and actual impact are unverified.
scenarios.attackPath: anonymous caller controls a request -> untrusted input crosses a boundary without validation at browser-to-Express API -> potential trust-boundary confusion or unsafe data flow.
scenarios.applicabilityRationale: The source inventory indicates this component exists; this particular attack path was not executed.
scenarios.safeValidationMethod: Trace source and, only with a verified local target, send a bounded synthetic request; do not use external systems.
scenarios.expectedSecureBehavior: Every trust transition authenticates the principal, validates data, enforces least privilege, and records only necessary evidence.
scenarios.requiredEvidence: Sanitized request/response or test assertion for browser-to-Express API; source and test references; cleanup proof for any authorized write.
scenarios.riskRationale: MEDIUM describes potential impact if this control fails; likelihood and exposure are unverified.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Document the boundary and enforce explicit validation, authorization, and failure behavior at its receiving component.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Add a focused unit/API test for the boundary and an isolated integration test when prerequisites are met.
scenarios.residualRisk: Unquantified until tested with required identity and environment.

scenarios.title: backup exists but cannot restore independently at PostgreSQL backup artifacts when operator responds to corruption
scenarios.domain: Backup restoration, rollback, migrations and operational recovery
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: unrestorable backup, irreversible migration, missing operator, or unsafe recovery
scenarios.potentialImpact: Potential high-class impact to affected data, identity, or service; reachability and actual impact are unverified.
scenarios.attackPath: operator responds to corruption -> backup exists but cannot restore independently at PostgreSQL backup artifacts -> potential unrestorable backup, irreversible migration, missing operator, or unsafe recovery.
scenarios.applicabilityRationale: Preview/database is stopped or synthetic credentials and supported reset procedure are unavailable.
scenarios.safeValidationMethod: Review runbooks and test only on a separate disposable restore target with authorization; no restore is attempted.
scenarios.expectedSecureBehavior: Recovery uses isolated target, verified artifact, defined RPO/RTO, integrity checks, named operators, and controlled return to service.
scenarios.requiredEvidence: Sanitized request/response or test assertion for PostgreSQL backup artifacts; source and test references; cleanup proof for any authorized write.
scenarios.riskRationale: HIGH describes potential impact if this control fails; likelihood and exposure are unverified.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Create encrypted backups and rehearse independent restore/rollback with post-restore invariants.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Restore to a separate disposable DB and record integrity, timing, and sign-off.
scenarios.residualRisk: Unquantified until tested with required identity and environment.

scenarios.domain: Additional project-specific risks and multi-step attack chains
scenarios.title: Example bootstrap password accepted through fresh local initialization
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: predictable bootstrap credential
scenarios.preconditions: Operator leaves the documented example value and initializes a fresh non-production database with a reachable admin interface.
scenarios.attackerPrivileges: Unauthenticated; must reach admin login and know public example text.
scenarios.potentialImpact: Unauthorized local administrator access.
scenarios.attackPath: Copied sample -> length-only local check -> bootstrap stores password hash -> reachable login accepts predictable credential.
scenarios.riskRationale: Pre-fix source accepted the sample by length; shared validation now rejects it and its regression passes.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Retain shared validation; separately rotate any existing account through an approved procedure.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: server/adminPassword.test.js rejects example prefixes and accepts a synthetic passphrase.
scenarios.retestStatus: PASS — regression test executed; live login not tested.
scenarios.residualRisk: Existing credentials remain unchanged; live authentication is blocked.
scenarios.applicabilityRationale: Chain is grounded in identified Shopademia source or prior local-preview evidence; external reachability is not assumed.
scenarios.safeValidationMethod: Use source/test evidence or authorized isolated reproduction only; external and destructive steps are prohibited.
scenarios.expectedSecureBehavior: Break the earliest feasible link with least privilege, explicit rotation, and recoverable operation.
scenarios.requiredEvidence: Sanitized source/test output; runtime requires verified target identity, synthetic identity, and cleanup evidence.

scenarios.title: Secret-bearing PowerShell launch text permits local credential or signing-key disclosure
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: secret exposure and credential/session compromise chain

scenarios.preconditions: A local observer can read parent command text and at least one value remains valid or is reused.
scenarios.attackerPrivileges: Local same-account or sufficiently privileged process observer.

scenarios.riskRationale: Prior investigation observed secret-bearing command text; reuse outside the synthetic preview is unknown.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Rotate each affected local value through supported procedures, revoke dependent sessions, and use protected configuration.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Launch with synthetic canaries and assert absence from command text, logs, and artifacts.

scenarios.residualRisk: Treat previously exposed values as compromised until rotated and scoped.

scenarios.domain: Additional project-specific risks and multi-step attack chains
scenarios.title: Environment password change gives false assurance because bootstrap is insert-only
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: ineffective credential rotation and stale account state
scenarios.asset: ADMIN_PASSWORD -> initializeDatabase -> admin_credentials ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
scenarios.preconditions: Administrator row exists and operator changes environment expecting it to replace the stored credential.
scenarios.attackerPrivileges: Operator can edit local config; attacker may know a previous credential.
scenarios.potentialImpact: Old password remains valid after an assumed rotation.
scenarios.attackPath: Operator changes variable -> hash is generated -> insert conflicts on singleton row -> existing password hash remains unchanged.
scenarios.riskRationale: Insert-only behavior is present in source; no supported reset path was established and no login was attempted.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Document an approved reset that updates credential state and session version; do not overwrite blindly.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Isolated DB test proves reset changes hash, bumps session version, and rejects old sessions.
scenarios.residualRisk: Live credential state and exposure duration are unknown.

scenarios.domain: Additional project-specific risks and multi-step attack chains
scenarios.title: JWT rotation and derived MFA encryption key can strand authenticator state
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: cryptographic key coupling and lifecycle failure
scenarios.preconditions: Non-production TOTP is enrolled while dedicated MFA key is unset and JWT key rotates without re-encryption.
scenarios.attackerPrivileges: Operator changes signing configuration; no attacker privilege needed for availability failure.
scenarios.potentialImpact: MFA secret decryption/login or recovery can fail.
scenarios.attackPath: MFA key derives from JWT -> TOTP is encrypted -> JWT rotates -> derived key changes -> decrypt fails.
scenarios.riskRationale: Fallback derivation is in source; enrollment state and rotation were not checked live.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Use a stable dedicated MFA key and versioned decrypt/re-encrypt rotation before retiring old key.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Test existing MFA state across planned key rotation and separately verify session invalidation.
scenarios.residualRisk: Enrollment state in stopped preview is unknown.
scenarios.applicabilityRationale: Chain is grounded in identified Shopademia source or prior local-preview evidence; external reachability is not assumed.

scenarios.title: Compromised deployment credential combines with destructive sync to alter remote files
scenarios.vulnerabilityClass: CI deployment authority and destructive synchronization chain
scenarios.asset: GitHub Actions deploy job -> SSH key -> cPanel target -> rsync --delete
scenarios.preconditions: Deploy gate is enabled and credential is compromised/mis-scoped or destination ownership is wrong.
scenarios.attackerPrivileges: Deployment credential/workflow control or authorized operator.
scenarios.potentialImpact: Remote application files may be replaced or deleted, causing outage or code compromise.
scenarios.attackPath: Deployment obtains SSH authority -> sync has delete semantics -> wrong target or malicious artifact reaches job -> remote files change before health check.
scenarios.riskRationale: Workflow source shows a gated job and delete sync; target ownership, credentials, protections, and recovery were not verified.
scenarios.remediationRecommendation: Verify approvals, ownership, least-privilege SSH, artifact provenance, and rollback before enabling deploy.
scenarios.regressionTestMethod: Rehearse to a disposable target with scoped tree and rollback; never use production secrets.
scenarios.retestStatus: BLOCKED — authorization and isolated target required.
scenarios.residualRisk: Runtime deployment controls remain unverified.
